is.t: JVM arguments: command line only, not YAML (documented: from the docs and launchers; suggested: beyond them)
The heap computed above. When: always. [documented]
The whole heap reserved and committed from the start: no growth pauses, and RSS is known from day one. When: a server. [suggested]

ZGC pauses under a millisecond whatever the heap; G1 costs less on a small heap. Measured: ZGC doubled RSS at the same -Xmx and stalled allocations at 200,000 positions; choose G1 (Collector) when RAM is tight. When: heap ≥ 16 GB: ZGC; Java 21 needs -XX:+ZGenerational. [documented]
ZGC collects early to stay under 80% of the heap (planned in the docs); G1's periodic collection returns unused memory. When: ZGC: 0.8 × heap; G1: always. [documented]
The docs give no pause goal; G1's default (200 ms) stays. When: not set. [documented]
Keeps 4-byte references above 32 GB, at the cost of padding objects to 16 bytes; or stay at 31g. When: heap over 31 GB, up to 64 GB. [suggested]
Smaller object headers, a little less heap. When: Java 25 only (21 refuses to start with it). [documented]
Not proposed by the docs: a slow start, and the whole heap committed at once. When: not set. [documented]
Caps direct buffers (the default cap is the heap's size). When: always. [documented]
Returns freed native memory to the system every minute. When: Java 21.0.1 and later. [documented]
Stops each thread keeping a large temporary direct buffer after a read. When: always. [documented]
Lets jcmd split native memory by category; a few per cent of overhead. When: always. [documented]
A ceiling well above the 131 MB measured, so a class leak fails loudly instead of growing; the code cache keeps its default. When: always. [suggested]
A heap dump when the heap runs out, under the data folder; the disk lines keep room for it. When: always. [documented]
A rotated GC log (5 × 20 MB). When: always. [documented]
Native libraries unpack and temporary files go under the data folder. When: always. [documented]
The Parquet footer cache computed above. When: always. [documented]
The byte safety net never closes a date read in the last 120 s (closing it would reload it at once). When: always. [documented]
-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full is a diagnostic only; the scheduler's parallelism keeps its default (the cores). When: not set. [documented]
The server jar's manifest already grants native access; no --add-opens is needed. When: not set with -jar. [documented]
Two malloc arenas, not one per busy thread: about 500 MB less RSS measured. When: Linux (glibc) only. [documented]
